model_interpretation.claim: A two-shuffle XOR butterfly over the four shared warp totals may reduce cross-warp combine work relative to the prior five-step warp reduction or serial lane-0 sum. This changes only the block-local combine while retaining 128-element tiles, recursive host stages, and modulo-2^32 partials; the full-program measurements do not establish that local reduction is the bottleneck.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Replaced the modulo/shared-memory reduction tree with five warp-local shuffle-down additions, one shared unsigned total per warp, and a two-stage XOR butterfly across the four totals in warp zero.","Used unsigned modulo-2^32 addition for all partial sums and mapped each residue to an in-range signed int before storing it, so recursive stages recover the same residue without out-of-range signed conversion.","Kept 128-thread blocks, zero-filled tail handling, the existing alternating scratch-bank offsets, recursive host launches, ABI, and default-stream ordering; writes zero asynchronously for n <= 0."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Keeping the selected parent's 2048-element tile fixed isolates a different finalization strategy: each CTA writes a 64-bit partial, then the last CTA uses a fenced counter to finalize them in the same kernel, replacing the separate partial-reduction kernel. The output counter must be zeroed first on the default stream, so the saved reduction-kernel launch may or may not offset the memset and counter/finalizer work.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Keep the 2048-element tile and 128-thread shared-memory CTA reduction, so the changed large-input strategy can be compared with the selected parent without changing grain size.","Replace the separate second reduction kernel with last-CTA finalization: each CTA writes a volatile 64-bit partial, fences before incrementing a per-call output counter, and the last CTA reduces the partials.","Initialize the counter with a default-stream asynchronous memset before the large-input kernel; retain the small-input path, empty sum behavior, bounded tails, and 64-bit intermediate sums."]}

model_interpretation.claim: The earlier full-cooperative candidate passed correctness but measured 0.762 ms versus the 46.244 μs baseline. This experiment tests whether limiting the cooperative grid to at most four resident CTAs per SM reduces grid-barrier and partial-handling costs, while retaining the ordinary path below 1<<20 to avoid cooperative setup costs on smaller inputs. The reduced grid may lower throughput; no speedup is assumed.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cu"],"retained":["Replace the previous maximum-occupancy cooperative grid with a grid capped at four occupancy-verified CTAs per SM, using grid-stride input processing and a cooperative grid barrier before CTA 0 reduces the fully written partials.","Use the cooperative path only for n >= 1<<20; preserve a conventional multi-kernel fallback when it is smaller, unavailable, or rejected at launch.","Perform reduction stages with unsigned 32-bit additions to avoid signed-overflow intermediate arithmetic, and write zero for n <= 0."]}

items.subject: Warp-first block reduction
items.objective: Using AB-MCTS, isolate the block-local reduction mechanism: replace the modulo/shared-memory tree with a warp-first reduction and cross-warp combine while retaining the 128-element tile and recursive host-stage structure where feasible. Do not assume signed int32 partial sums are safe merely because the final sum fits; use exact intermediate arithmetic (e.g. wider partials) or a rigorously correct modular representation and final conversion. Preserve tail handling, ABI, default stream, scratch bounds, and every valid n (including n=0 if valid under the official domain). Report failed attempts, correctness results, and repeated full-program timings; this is a hypothesis about local reduction cost, not a proven bottleneck.

items.subject: Fewer launches with a two-pass hierarchy
items.objective: Using AB-MCTS, focus on the conventional multi-kernel hierarchy: vary tile/grain size and partial-count/finalization strategy to test lower-launch-count designs, including but not assuming a two-pass design wins. Avoid repeating a broad warp-reduction sweep already assigned to T1; use a straightforward correct CTA reduction unless tuning it is necessary to realize a hierarchy. Preserve exact arithmetic for all valid inputs, including safe intermediate sums, uninitialized scratch, tails, ABI, and default-stream behavior. If n=0 is valid, produce the empty sum. Report failures, correctness, and repeated full-program timings, then compare against the supplied baseline without treating one launch-count hypothesis as the result.

items.subject: Single-launch cooperative reduction
items.objective: Using AB-MCTS, investigate the distinct cooperative single-kernel path: resident CTAs compute grid-stride partials, synchronize grid-wide, and one CTA writes the result. The CUDA 12.6.3 guide documents the needed cooperative launch/grid synchronization, but that does not establish effective runtime support or performance on this measured target; validate the actual launch and include host-side setup/query costs in full-program timings. Ensure residency-safe configuration, exact intermediate arithmetic, no reliance on initialized scratch or atomics, and correctness for every valid n (including n=0 if valid). Record unsupported, incorrect, or slower attempts; only return a correctly validated candidate.
